title: Harborlight Notes
intro: Teal enamel mug by the map, compass badge to dawn,
Mist on the ridge, harbor breathing pale beyond.
Mira writes “Harborlight Camp” on a waiting page,
Papa Bear checks weather, trail, return-time range.
verse1: He’s called Papa Bear—patient guide, rust-colored coat,
“Torch, water, spare layer?” Mira checks every note.
Two maps, same route; if weather shifts, they turn,
No grand view is worth what a bad shortcut burns.
At the trail board, she takes a picture, checks print,
Marker says sheltered ridge; they follow its intent.
A bright hillside tempts—still, they pass that gleam,
The agreed path holds when the easy path beams.
At the overlook, footbridge changes in the air:
Short from the shore, long from the height up there.
“Which drawing’s right?” Neither; she labels her stand,
Two honest angles held in the same small hand.
Tent on level ground, clear path, tripod feet checked,
Mug low on the table, notebook clipped at the edge.
Cloud crosses one star; she wants all sky, all bright,
He says, “Write what’s here.” Pale sky, breeze, one light.
chorus1: Harborlight notes—don’t name it too soon,
Hold the map to the mug, let the cloud cross the moon.
Harborlight notes—what did your own eyes find?
Describe the evidence before you decide the sign.
verse2: Dark settles in; Mira lowers lantern’s warm ring,
Shield turned toward the table—enough light for things.
Beyond that little circle, ridge separates from sky,
Papa Bear waits till sun-glow leaves the eyepiece dry.
They trade turns at the lens; she calls it “a bright point,”
No distance invented to enlarge the joint.
“What changed since last look?” Cloud moved from its place,
Harbor lamps sharpened; pale band thinned from the face.
Then—a brief streak cuts open sky while both heads lift,
Gone before a full sketch could hold that swift shift.
Direction, rough time, only a moment: ink it plain,
Leave room for “uncertain,” don’t make a glimpse a claim.
Quiet takes the campsite; shared attention runs deep,
Mug warming her hands while the dark learns to keep.
Last line on the page, no spectacle in the view:
Waiting gave us something hurry would have flew through.
chorus2: Harborlight notes—don’t name it too soon,
Hold the map to the mug, let the cloud cross the moon.
Harborlight notes—the streak was brief, not a sign,
Describe the evidence before you decide the sign.
verse3: Before bed, they match each page against the plan:
Place, weather, time, observer—so another person can.
Sketches marked as sketches; uncertain stays unsure,
A clear record travels farther than a boastful report.
Morning: Mira counts the low table’s little row:
Mug, notebook, clip, lantern, telescope case—go.
Papa Bear checks the campsite, scraps and loose gear,
They leave it as they found it, path open and clear.
Same marked trail down toward the harbor’s blue,
At the overlook, the bridge wears another view.
Morning light makes a third small drawing appear,
She doesn’t erase the first—why delete what was clear?
Position and light made each true outline bend,
Not rivals in a fight—three witnesses, friends.
Back at the window, mug beside folded map,
Four pages, three bridge sketches; the journey’s packed.
No dramatic tale required for the habit to start:
Say what the evidence is—then let meaning take part.
bridge: Mira: “The bridge changed.” Papa Bear: “Or where we stand.”
She clips the page shut, mug steadying the plan.
Same harbor. Different light. Nothing to erase.
The record keeps the question—and makes room for the next place.
chorus3: Harborlight notes—now the title means more:
Three bridge sketches, one route, and a clean campsite floor.
Harborlight notes—carry this into every sign:
Describe the evidence before you decide the sign.
